sentences.text: Es war einmal ein kleines Mädchen.
sentences.translation: Once upon a time there was a little girl.

words.grammar: fixed fairy-tale opener · war = Präteritum of sein
das Mädchen · one of the few neuter nouns for a female person

sentences.text: Sie trug immer eine rote Kappe.
sentences.translation: She always wore a red cap.

words.grammar: tragen · Präteritum · strong verb: tragen → trug
die Kappe · gives the character her name

sentences.translation: That's why everyone called her Little Red Riding Hood.

words.grammar: connecting adverb · triggers inverted word order: Deshalb nannten (verb before subject)
nennen · Präteritum · irregular: nennen → nannten

sentences.text: Eines Tages sagte die Mutter: "Bring der Großmutter einen Kuchen."
sentences.translation: One day the mother said: "Bring grandmother a cake."

words.grammar: genitive time expression · fixed phrase, worth learning as a chunk
bringen · imperative (du-form) · der Großmutter = dative (recipient), einen Kuchen = accusative (object)

sentences.text: Rotkäppchen ging allein durch den Wald.
sentences.translation: Little Red Riding Hood walked alone through the forest.

words.grammar: manner adverb, modifies ging
durch + accusative (movement through) · der Wald → den Wald

sentences.text: Im Wald traf sie einen Wolf.
sentences.translation: In the forest she met a wolf.

words.grammar: treffen · Präteritum · strong verb: treffen → traf
der Wolf · accusative after traf: einen Wolf

sentences.translation: The wolf asked: "Where are you going?"

words.grammar: question word (wohin) directly followed by the verb, then the subject · no extra 'do' word, unlike English

sentences.translation: Little Red Riding Hood told him everything.

words.grammar: erzählen · Präteritum · regular weak verb: -te ending
indefinite pronoun · accusative, direct object of erzählte

sentences.text: Der Wolf lief schnell zum Haus der Großmutter.
sentences.translation: The wolf ran quickly to grandmother's house.

words.grammar: laufen · Präteritum · strong verb: laufen → lief
zu + dem → zum · der Großmutter = genitive, showing possession (grandmother's)

sentences.text: Als Rotkäppchen ankam, sagte sie: "Großmutter, du hast so große Augen!"
sentences.translation: When Little Red Riding Hood arrived, she said: "Grandmother, what big eyes you have!"

words.grammar: als = subordinating conjunction for a single past event · sends the verb to the end of its clause: 'Als Rotkäppchen ankam'
das Auge · plural: Augen · große = strong adjective ending (no article before it here)

sentences.text: Zum Glück kam ein Jäger und rettete beide.
sentences.translation: Luckily a hunter came and rescued both of them.

words.grammar: fixed adverbial phrase · zu + dem Glück (the luck) → zum Glück
retten · Präteritum · regular weak verb
refers back to Rotkäppchen and the Großmutter · accusative, object of rettete

sentences.text: Am Ende waren alle froh und aßen den Kuchen zusammen.
sentences.translation: In the end everyone was happy and ate the cake together.

words.grammar: an + dem → am · fixed time expression
predicate adjective after waren · no ending needed in this position

grammarPoints.exampleSentence: Es war einmal ein kleines Mädchen. Sie trug immer eine rote Kappe.
grammarPoints.explanation: German fairy tales are almost always told in the Präteritum (simple past), even though everyday spoken German prefers the Perfekt. Recognising common strong-verb forms like war, trug, traf, lief and kam is a key reading skill, even at A1 — you don't need to produce them yet, just recognise them.

grammarPoints.exampleSentence: Als Rotkäppchen ankam, sagte sie: "Großmutter, du hast so große Augen!"
grammarPoints.explanation: 'Als' introduces a subordinate clause describing one specific past event — here, the moment she arrived. The verb moves to the end of the als-clause (ankam). This is different from 'wenn', which is used for repeated or future events.
